userSnippets.name: Pac-Man Tile Collection
userSnippets.code:
; Pac-Man Style Tile Collection System for MSX
; Optimized for MSX hardware limitations
; Uses: DE = Player position, HL = Screen map address

COLLECT_TILES:
    ; Input: DE = Player X,Y position (D=X, E=Y)
    ; Input: HL = Screen map base address
    ; Output: A = Number of items collected
    ; Destroys: BC, DE, HL
    
    push bc
    push de
    push hl
    
    ld a, 0                    ; Initialize collection counter
    ld (COLLECTION_COUNT), a
    
    ; Convert pixel position to tile coordinates
    ld a, d                    ; Player X
    srl a                      ; Divide by 2
    srl a                      ; Divide by 4
    srl a                      ; Divide by 8 (assuming 8x8 tiles)
    ld d, a                    ; D = Tile X
    
    ld a, e                    ; Player Y  
    srl a                      ; Divide by 2
    srl a                      ; Divide by 4
    srl a                      ; Divide by 8
    ld e, a                    ; E = Tile Y
    
    ; Calculate tile address: HL + (Y * MAP_WIDTH) + X
    ld a, e                    ; Y coordinate
    ld b, 0
    ld c, 32                   ; MAP_WIDTH (assuming 32 tiles wide)
    call MULTIPLY_AC           ; A = Y * MAP_WIDTH
    
    add a, d                   ; A = (Y * MAP_WIDTH) + X
    ld c, a
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc                 ; HL points to tile at player position
    
    ; Check if current tile is collectible
    ld a, (hl)                 ; Load tile ID
    cp DOT_TILE_ID             ; Compare with dot tile
    jr z, COLLECT_DOT
    cp POWERUP_TILE_ID         ; Compare with power-up tile
    jr z, COLLECT_POWERUP
    cp FRUIT_TILE_ID           ; Compare with fruit tile
    jr z, COLLECT_FRUIT
    jr END_COLLECTION          ; Nothing to collect
    
COLLECT_DOT:
    ld a, EMPTY_TILE_ID        ; Replace with empty tile
    ld (hl), a
    ld a, (SCORE)              ; Load current score
    add a, 10                  ; Add 10 points for dot
    ld (SCORE), a
    ld a, (DOT_COUNT)          ; Increment dot counter
    inc a
    ld (DOT_COUNT), a
    call PLAY_DOT_SOUND        ; Play collection sound
    jr INCREMENT_COLLECTION

COLLECT_POWERUP:
    ld a, EMPTY_TILE_ID
    ld (hl), a
    ld a, (SCORE)
    add a, 50                  ; Add 50 points for power-up
    ld (SCORE), a
    ld a, 1
    ld (POWER_MODE), a         ; Activate power mode
    call PLAY_POWERUP_SOUND
    jr INCREMENT_COLLECTION

COLLECT_FRUIT:
    ld a, EMPTY_TILE_ID
    ld (hl), a
    ld a, (SCORE)
    add a, 100                 ; Add 100 points for fruit
    ld (SCORE), a
    ld a, (FRUIT_COUNT)
    inc a
    ld (FRUIT_COUNT), a
    call PLAY_FRUIT_SOUND
    jr INCREMENT_COLLECTION

INCREMENT_COLLECTION:
    ld a, (COLLECTION_COUNT)
    inc a
    ld (COLLECTION_COUNT), a

END_COLLECTION:
    ld a, (COLLECTION_COUNT)   ; Return collection count in A
    
    pop hl
    pop de
    pop bc
    ret

; Helper routine: Multiply A * C, result in A
MULTIPLY_AC:
    ld b, 0
    ld h, b
    ld l, a
    ld d, h
    ld e, l
    add hl, hl                 ; HL = A * 2
    jr nc, MUL_NO_CARRY1
    inc de
MUL_NO_CARRY1:
    add hl, hl                 ; HL = A * 4
    jr nc, MUL_NO_CARRY2
    inc de
MUL_NO_CARRY2:
    add hl, hl                 ; HL = A * 8
    jr nc, MUL_NO_CARRY3
    inc de
MUL_NO_CARRY3:
    add hl, hl                 ; HL = A * 16
    jr nc, MUL_NO_CARRY4
    inc de
MUL_NO_CARRY4:
    add hl, hl                 ; HL = A * 32
    ld a, l
    ret

; Sound effect stubs (implement based on your sound system)
PLAY_DOT_SOUND:
    ; Play dot collection sound
    ret
    
PLAY_POWERUP_SOUND:
    ; Play power-up sound
    ret
    
PLAY_FRUIT_SOUND:
    ; Play fruit collection sound
    ret

; Data section
DOT_TILE_ID:        EQU 1      ; Tile ID for collectible dots
POWERUP_TILE_ID:    EQU 2      ; Tile ID for power-ups
FRUIT_TILE_ID:      EQU 3      ; Tile ID for bonus fruits
EMPTY_TILE_ID:      EQU 0      ; Tile ID for empty space

; Memory variables
COLLECTION_COUNT:   DB 0       ; Items collected this frame
SCORE:              DW 0       ; Player score
DOT_COUNT:          DB 0       ; Total dots collected
FRUIT_COUNT:        DB 0       ; Total fruits collected
POWER_MODE:         DB 0       ; Power-up mode active flag

articles.title: Welcome to MSX Retro IDE
articles.content:
Welcome!

This IDE is designed to help you create games for the MSX (MSX1/MSX2) platform.

Key features include:

  • Visual Tile Editor with Tile Banks support
  • Sprite Editor with animation support
  • Screen Map Editor with Effect Zones and HUD config
  • Integrated Z80 Code Editor with snippets
  • World Map Editor for connecting screens
  • GameFlow and State Machine systems for logic
  • Entity Component System (ECS)
  • PT3 Music Tracker and Sound FX Editors
  • Font Editor

Use the File Explorer on the left to manage your assets. Create new assets using the Toolbar at the top.

Select an asset to open its dedicated editor. Properties for the selected asset or element will appear in the Properties Panel on the right.

articles.title: Toolbar Overview
articles.content:
Toolbar Guide

The main toolbar provides quick access to common actions:

  • New Project: Clears current work and sets up a new project structure (main.asm, etc.).
  • Load/Save/Save As: Standard project file operations (saves as .json).
  • New Asset: Dropdown to create State Machines, Tiles, Sprites, Fonts, Screen Maps, World Maps, GameFlows, Tile Banks, Sound FX, Music Tracks, and Code files.
  • Undo/Redo: Reverts or reapplies recent changes.
  • System Tools: Access World View, Component Definitions, and Entity Templates.
  • Configure: Dropdown for IDE settings (Data Output, Autosave, Theme, ASM Compiler, MSX Emulator).
  • Help: Opens this Help & Documentation viewer.

articles.title: Sprite Editor Basics
articles.content:
Sprite Editor Basics

The Sprite Editor allows you to create and animate game characters and objects.

Key Areas:

  • Left Panel (Tools & Palette):
    • Tools: Switch between Draw and Erase (uses background color).
    • Active Brush: Select one of the 4 sprite palette colors to draw with.
    • Define Sprite Colors: Assign MSX colors to the 4 sprite palette slots and the sprite's background color. Click a slot, then pick from the main MSX Palette Panel.
  • Center Panel (Pixel Grid): The main drawing canvas for the current frame.
  • Right Panel (Frame Management & Preview):
    • Animation Preview: Shows a small preview of the current frame.
    • Frame Control: Add, duplicate, delete, or navigate between animation frames.
    • Transform Frame: Tools to shift, rotate (square sprites), clear, or contract the current frame.
    • Generate Explosion: A utility to create animated explosion sprite sequences.

Tips:

  • Sprites use a 4-color palette + 1 background color for transparency/erasing.
  • MSX sprites have hardware limitations (e.g., max sprites per line). Keep this in mind for your game design.
  • Use the "Export ASM" button to get Z80 assembly data for your sprite.

articles.title: Screen Editor Basics
articles.content:
Screen Editor Basics

The Screen Editor is used to design game levels and layouts by placing tiles.

Layers:

The editor supports multiple layers:

  • Background: The main visual layer for your map.
  • Collision: Defines areas where the player/entities cannot pass. Tiles placed here act as collision markers.
  • Effects: Used to define rectangular zones for gameplay effects (e.g., water, ice, custom gravity, sprite concealment). Edit properties of these zones in the Properties Panel.
  • Entities: Place game entities like player start, enemies, items.

Tools & Panels:

  • Tileset Panel (Left): Shows available tiles. Click a tile to select it for drawing on Background/Collision layers. Hidden when 'Effects' layer is active.
  • Entity Types Panel (Right, when Entity layer active): Lists your configured Entity Templates. Select one to place instances on the map.
  • Properties Panel (Right): Shows properties of the selected map, entity instance, or effect zone.
  • Active Area: Defines the playable portion of the screen map. Areas outside can be used for HUD elements. Editable via input fields in the toolbar.
  • Toolbar (Screen Editor): Contains layer selectors, zoom, active area inputs, HUD editor button, and export options. When 'Effects' layer is active, a "New Zone" button appears after selecting an area.

Effect Zones:

On the 'Effects' layer, you can draw alternate tiles and define rectangular trigger zones. Each zone has:

  • A name.
  • Position (x,y) and Size (width, height) in grid cells.
  • An Effect Type: the runtime behavior for the zone, such as secretZone or wind.
  • Optional per-effect parameters, for example wind direction and strength.

SCREEN 2 Specifics:

When in SCREEN 2 mode:

  • Tiles are typically 8x8 character blocks.
  • Tile Banks become crucial for managing character codes and colors. Assign your 8x8 tiles to banks. The Screen Editor will use these bank assignments to resolve tile placements into character codes for export.
  • The editor's base cell dimension is 8x8.

articles.title: HUD Configuration
articles.content:
HUD Configuration

The HUD (Heads-Up Display) mode is available from the Screen Editor toolbar. It allows you to place UI elements like Score, Lives, and text on parts of the screen outside the active gameplay area.

Features:

  • Add specific HUD elements (Score, HighScore, Lives, Custom Text, etc.).
  • In MSX SCREEN 2, you can import an external screen as a background template for your HUD.
  • Assign TileBanks to specific screen sectors to manage character sets appropriately over 3 sectors.

articles.title: Introduction to ECS
articles.content:
Entity Component System (ECS)

Mideas uses an ECS architecture to manage game objects. This involves two main concepts:

Component Definitions

Found under System Tools. Here you define reusable data structures (e.g., Position, Health, Renderable). A component defines properties like byte, word, boolean, or references to other assets.

Entity Templates

Found under System Tools. An entity template combines multiple components to form a specific type of game object (e.g., Player, Enemy). You assign default values to the components included in the template.

Entity Instances

Once you have created an Entity Template, you can place instances of it onto a Screen Map using the Screen Editor's Entity layer. Each instance can optionally override the default component values.

articles.title: World Map Editor
articles.content:
World Map Editor

The World Map editor allows you to visually connect multiple Screen Maps to form your game's world layout.

  • Nodes: Each node represents a Screen Map instance.
  • Connections: Draw lines between nodes to specify how screens connect (North, South, East, West).
  • Start Screen: Right-click a node to set it as the starting screen of the game.

articles.title: State Machine Editor
articles.content:
State Machine Editor

State Machines define complex behavior for your game entities without writing code manually.

  • States: Represent a behavior phase (e.g., Idle, Walking, Attacking). Each state can execute Z80 logic.
  • Transitions: Define conditions under which an entity moves from one state to another (e.g., If KeyPressed(Right) -> WalkRight).
  • Actions: Assign specific actions when entering, exiting, or running a state.

articles.title: Global Variables
articles.content:
Global Variables

Global Variables allow you to define system-wide parameters (like Score, Lives, Goal status) that can be accessed by both GameFlow logic and State Machines.

You can create variables of different types (boolean, byte, word) and reference them conditionally to branch your game's logic flow.

articles.title: PT3 Music Tracker
articles.content:
PT3 Music Tracker

The PT3 Music Tracker allows you to compose music for the MSX PSG (AY-3-8910) or SCC chips.

  • Patterns: Compose repeating blocks of music across 3 channels (PSG) or 5 channels (SCC).
  • Instruments: Define sound properties such as volume/tone envelopes and hardware shapes.
  • Ornaments: Define pitch modulations.
  • You can use your PC keyboard as a piano to input notes when the tracker has focus.

articles.title: Sound FX Editor
articles.content:
Sound FX Editor

Create sound effects using a step-based sequence for the PSG chip.

  • Define sequences of tone and noise periods alongside volume levels.
  • Can utilize hardware envelopes for specific effects.
  • Useful for jumps, explosions, shots, and other gameplay sounds.

articles.title: Introduction to GameFlow
articles.content:
GameFlow System

GameFlow is the game flow control system in Mideas MSX. It allows you to create your game's logic using a visual system based on nodes and connections, without writing ASM code.

What can you do with GameFlow?

  • Create main and in-game menus
  • Add victory, defeat, and credits screens
  • Implement conditional logic (if/then/else)
  • Display text and dialogues
  • Apply visual transition effects
  • Control music and sounds
  • Manage levels and worlds
  • Implement pause and wait systems

How does it work?

The game starts at the Start node and flows from node to node following the connections you define. Each node executes a specific action and then proceeds to the next connected node.

Start → Menu → WorldLink (Game Loop) → End

Basic Concepts

Nodes

A node is a unit of game logic. Each node has:

  • Type: Defines what the node does (menu, text, game, etc.)
  • Data: Node-specific configuration
  • Connections: Links to other nodes

Connections

Connections determine the game flow:

  • DEFAULT: Linear connection (next node)
  • THEN/ELSE: Conditional connections
  • OPTION_0 to OPTION_5: Menu options

Global Variables

You can use variables to control flow:

  • score: Player score
  • lives: Remaining lives
  • level: Current level
  • Custom variables

articles.title: Basic Node Types
articles.content:
Basic Node Types

1. Start (Beginning)

Description: Initial game node. Must always be the first node.

Properties: No data, only DEFAULT connection

Start → (next node)

2. End (Finish)

Description: Shows an end screen and waits for player input.

Properties:

  • endType: Screen type (0-3)
    • 0: Victory (VICTORY!)
    • 1: Defeat (GAME OVER)
    • 2: Credits (CREDITS)
    • 3: Custom message
  • message: Custom message (only if endType=3)

Behavior: Displays screen, waits for FIRE or ESC, game ends

3. Restart

Description: Restarts the game from the beginning.

Properties: No data, no connections (restarts directly)

Behavior: Jumps to init_rom (complete reset)

4. WorldLink (World/Level)

Description: Starts main gameplay. Executes the world's game loop.

Properties:

  • worldId: ID of the world to load
  • screenId: Initial screen ID
  • DEFAULT connection (executed when world ends)

Behavior:

  • Loads world and entities
  • Executes game loop (ECS + State Machines)
  • Infinite loop until gameflow_exit_requested = 1
  • When finished, continues to DEFAULT connection

How to exit: Use a component/behavior that sets gameflow_exit_requested = 1

5. SubMenu (Menu)

Description: Shows an interactive menu with options.

Properties:

  • title: Menu title
  • options: Array of strings (menu options)
  • OPTION_0 to OPTION_N connections (one per option)

Controls:

  • UP: Previous option
  • DOWN: Next option
  • FIRE: Select option

Behavior: Shows menu, player navigates, continues to node based on selected option

6. Text

Description: Shows text in the bottom area of the screen.

Properties:

  • text: Text to display
  • duration: Duration in frames (60 frames = 1 second)
    • If 0: Waits for player input
    • If >0: Waits N frames
  • DEFAULT connection (next node)

Behavior: Clears text area, shows centered text, waits duration OR input, continues to next node

articles.title: Advanced Node Types
articles.content:
Advanced Node Types

7. IfThenElse (Conditional)

Description: Evaluates a condition and chooses between two paths.

Properties:

  • variable: Variable to evaluate (e.g., "score", "lives")
  • value: Value to compare
  • operator: Comparison operator
    • "equals": Variable == Value
    • "greater": Variable > Value
    • "less": Variable < Value
    • "greaterOrEqual": Variable >= Value
    • "lessOrEqual": Variable <= Value
  • THEN and ELSE connections

Behavior:

  • Reads global variable
  • Compares with value using operator
  • If TRUE: Continues via THEN
  • If FALSE: Continues via ELSE

8. Transition

Description: Applies a visual transition effect.

Properties:

  • effectType: Effect type (0-4)
    • 0: Fade Out (~1.3s)
    • 1: Fade In (~1.3s)
    • 2: Flash (~0.5s)
    • 3: Wipe Down (~0.8s)
    • 4: Wipe Up (~0.8s)
  • DEFAULT connection (next node)

Behavior: Executes visual effect, automatically continues to next node

9. Music

Description: Controls music playback.

Properties:

  • command: Music command (0-3)
    • 0: Stop
    • 1: Play
    • 2: Pause
    • 3: Resume
  • trackId: Track ID (only for Play)
  • loop: Loop playback (only for Play)
  • DEFAULT connection (next node)

Behavior: Executes music command (PSG AY-3-8910), continues immediately, music plays in background

10. Group (Nested Flow)

Description: Executes a nested GameFlow sub-flow.

Properties:

  • subFlowStartNode: Start node ID of sub-flow
  • DEFAULT connection (next node after sub-flow)

Behavior: Saves current state on stack, executes complete sub-flow, restores state and continues

Use cases: Cutscenes, complex sub-menus, dialogue sequences, mini-games

11. Waypoint (Marker)

Description: Invisible node serving as a reference point.

Properties:

  • name: Waypoint name
  • DEFAULT connection (next node)

Behavior: Does nothing visible, continues immediately to next node

Use cases: Organize flow visually, return/save points, debugging

12. Globals (Global Variables)

Description: Modifies global variables.

Properties:

  • variable: Variable name
  • value: Value to assign
  • operation: Operation to perform
    • "set": Variable = Value
    • "add": Variable += Value
    • "subtract": Variable -= Value
  • DEFAULT connection (next node)

Behavior: Modifies global variable, continues immediately to next node

articles.title: Practical Examples
articles.content:
Practical Examples

Example 1: Simple Game

Start
  ↓
SubMenu (Main Menu)
  ├─ OPTION_0 (New Game) → Fade Out → WorldLink (Level 1) → Victory
  ├─ OPTION_1 (Continue) → WorldLink (Level 1)
  └─ OPTION_2 (Quit) → End (Thanks)

Example 2: Lives System

WorldLink (Game)
  ↓ (on death)
IfThenElse (lives == 0?)
  ├─ THEN → Game Over
  └─ ELSE → Globals (lives -= 1) → Flash → Restart Level

Example 3: Progressive Levels

Start
  ↓
Text ("LEVEL 1")
  ↓
WorldLink (Level 1)
  ↓
IfThenElse (score >= 500?)
  ├─ THEN → Text ("LEVEL 2") → WorldLink (Level 2) → Victory
  └─ ELSE → Game Over

Example 4: Menu with Music

Start
  ↓
Music (Play menu theme)
  ↓
SubMenu (Main Menu)
  ├─ New Game → Music (Stop) → Music (Play game theme) → WorldLink
  ├─ Settings → Group (Settings Flow) → Main Menu
  └─ Quit → Music (Stop) → End

Tips

  • Clear Flow: Keep your flow linear and understandable
  • Smooth Transitions: Use transition effects between scenes
  • Initialize Variables: Set initial values at the start
  • Complete Connections: Always define both THEN and ELSE branches
  • Music Management: Stop music before changing tracks

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.content:
Common Problems and Solutions

Problem 1: Menu doesn't respond

Symptoms: Menu shows but I can't navigate

Possible causes:

  • No connections defined for options
  • Joystick not connected correctly

Solution: Ensure all OPTION_N connections are defined in your SubMenu node

Problem 2: WorldLink never ends

Symptoms: Game stuck in infinite loop

Possible causes: gameflow_exit_requested is not set to 1

Solution: Ensure your code/behavior sets the exit flag when level completes

Problem 3: Transitions don't show

Symptoms: Transition effects don't appear

Possible causes:

  • Incorrect effectType (must be 0-4)
  • ASM code not compiled correctly

Solution: Verify effectType is within valid range (0-4)

Problem 4: Music doesn't play

Symptoms: Music command produces no sound

Possible causes:

  • Incorrect trackId (track doesn't exist)
  • Stop command called before

Solution: Verify track exists and Play command is used correctly

Problem 5: Variables don't update

Symptoms: Globals doesn't change variable values

Possible causes:

  • Incorrect variable name
  • Wrong operation

Solution: Use exact variable name and correct operation ("set", "add", or "subtract")

Problem 6: IfThenElse always goes ELSE

Symptoms: Condition never met

Possible causes:

  • Wrong operator
  • Variable not initialized
  • Incorrect comparison value

Solution: Verify operator and variable initialization

Valid operators: "equals", "greater", "less", "greaterOrEqual", "lessOrEqual"

Problem 7: Text appears cut off

Symptoms: Text doesn't show completely

Possible causes:

  • Text too long (max ~30 characters)
  • Unsupported characters

Solution: Limit text to 30 characters max, use only standard ASCII (A-Z, 0-9, basic punctuation)

Problem 8: ROM doesn't compile

Symptoms: glass.jar compilation error

Possible causes:

  • Nodes without required connections
  • Duplicate node IDs
  • References to non-existent nodes

Solution:

  • Verify all nodes have required connections
  • Ensure unique IDs for each node
  • Verify targets exist in node list

componentDefinitions.name: Position

properties.name: x
properties.description: Horizontal position (pixel units or grid units depending on context)

properties.name: y
properties.description: Vertical position

componentDefinitions.description: Defines an entity's 2D coordinates.

componentDefinitions.name: Carry
componentDefinitions.description: Configures how the entity carries objects (e.g., vertical offset above head).

properties.name: offset
properties.description: Vertical pixels between hero head and carried object (0 = pegado).

properties.name: carrySpriteAssetId
properties.description: Optional sprite to display while the entity is carrying another object.

componentDefinitions.name: Box
componentDefinitions.description: Marks this entity as a carriable box that can be picked up and moved.

properties.name: isCarriable
properties.description: Whether this box can be picked up by entities with comp_carry.

componentDefinitions.name: Renderable

properties.name: spriteAssetId
properties.description: ID of the sprite asset to render

properties.name: isVisible
properties.description: Whether the entity is currently visible

properties.name: layer
properties.description: Render layer (0=bg, 1=main, 2=fg)

componentDefinitions.description: Allows an entity to be drawn on screen using a sprite.

componentDefinitions.name: Behavior

properties.name: scriptAssetId
properties.description: ID of the behavior script to run

componentDefinitions.description: Attaches a behavior script to an entity.

componentDefinitions.name: AutoControlScript

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: Whether this scripted control component is active in tutorial/dialog/cutscene screens.

properties.name: startsOnScreenLoad
properties.description: Run the command list when the screen starts.

properties.name: loop
properties.description: Restart the command list after it finishes.

properties.name: defaultDialogueAssetId
properties.description: Optional Dialogue asset used by play_dialog, open_dialog, or write_line commands.

properties.name: idleSpriteAssetId
properties.description: Optional sprite to apply while the FakePlayer is waiting, talking, or finished.

properties.name: walkSpriteAssetId
properties.description: Optional sprite to apply while the FakePlayer is executing movement commands.

properties.name: scriptFormat
properties.description: Script runtime format: commands for readable editor commands, eventString for compact FakePlayer event chains.

properties.name: eventString
properties.description: Compact FakePlayer event chain: x64 right, X64 left, y16 down, Y16 up, d1000 delay ms, o open dialog, w1 write dialogue line 1, s wait SPC, t wait text, k clear, c close.

properties.name: commands
properties.description: One command per line: move_right or move right pixels, jump, dash_right or dash right, grab_wall, release_wall, delay ms, wait seconds, play_dialog, open_dialog/open frame_dialog, write_line/write text index, wait_spc/wait SPC, wait_text/wait text, clear_dialog/clean, close_dialog.

componentDefinitions.description: Editor-only script data for FakePlayer/tutorial actors. It does not change the real Player control path.

componentDefinitions.name: Health
componentDefinitions.description: Manages health points for an entity.

componentDefinitions.name: Lifetime
componentDefinitions.description: Auto-destruye la entidad tras un tiempo determinado desde su creación.

properties.name: lifetimeMs
properties.description: Tiempo de vida en milisegundos. Si es 0 o vacío, no expira.

componentDefinitions.name: Jump
componentDefinitions.description: Manages jumping behavior for an entity.

properties.name: jumpPower
properties.description: Initial upward velocity or force.

properties.name: jumpSprite
properties.description: Sprite to use while jumping.

properties.name: maxJumps
properties.description: Number of jumps allowed before landing.

properties.name: currentJumpCount
properties.description: Current jump count.

properties.name: isJumping
properties.description: Is the entity currently jumping?

properties.name: requireKeyRelease
properties.description: If true, jump key must be released before jumping again.

componentDefinitions.name: Gravity
componentDefinitions.description: Applies gravitational force to an entity.

properties.name: strength
properties.description: Acceleration due to gravity.

properties.name: terminalVelocity
properties.description: Maximum falling speed.

componentDefinitions.name: Animation
componentDefinitions.description: Manages sprite animation sequences for an entity.

properties.name: currentAnimationName
properties.description: Name of the current animation (e.g., 'idle', 'walk').

properties.name: currentFrameIndex
properties.description: Current frame in the animation.

properties.name: animationSpeed
properties.description: Ticks/frames per animation update.

properties.name: loops
properties.description: Does the animation loop?

properties.name: isPlaying
properties.description: Is the animation currently playing?

properties.name: animateOnlyWhenMoving
properties.description: Only animate when entity has non-zero velocity (vx or vy).

componentDefinitions.name: Collision

properties.name: hitboxWidth
properties.description: Width of the collision bounding box.

properties.name: hitboxHeight
properties.description: Height of the collision bounding box.

properties.name: offsetX
properties.description: Horizontal offset of the hitbox from the entity's origin.

properties.name: offsetY
properties.description: Vertical offset of the hitbox from the entity's origin.

properties.name: collisionLayer
properties.description: Bitmask defining the entity's collision group (e.g., 1=player, 2=enemy).

properties.name: collidesWith
properties.description: Bitmask defining which layers this entity can collide with.

properties.name: isStatic
properties.description: If true, this entity is immovable and won't be pushed by collisions. Other entities will be pushed away when colliding with static entities.

properties.name: isTrigger
properties.description: If true, collision is detected for events but entities pass through each other (no physical pushback). Use for collectibles, checkpoints, damage zones. If false, entities push/separate on collision (solid collision).

componentDefinitions.description: Defines the physical shape and interaction rules for entity-to-entity collisions. Supports both solid (pushback) and trigger (overlap-only) collision modes.

componentDefinitions.name: Wall Collision

properties.name: hitboxWidth
properties.description: Width of the collision bounding box for wall detection.

properties.name: hitboxHeight
properties.description: Height of the collision bounding box for wall detection.

properties.name: offsetX
properties.description: Horizontal offset of the hitbox from the entity's origin.

properties.name: offsetY
properties.description: Vertical offset of the hitbox from the entity's origin.

properties.name: tileSize
properties.description: Size of tiles in the collision layer (usually 8x8 for MSX).

properties.name: stopOnCollision
properties.description: Whether to stop entity movement when hitting a wall.

componentDefinitions.description: Defines collision detection with solid tiles in the collision layer (walls, obstacles).

componentDefinitions.name: Wall Jump
componentDefinitions.description: Permite deslizarse por paredes y saltar/rebotar desde ellas con impulso horizontal y vertical configurables.

properties.name: horizontalPush
properties.description: Velocidad horizontal aplicada al saltar desde la pared.

properties.name: verticalImpulse
properties.description: Impulso vertical 8.8 aplicado al wall jump (1280 = #0500 de magnitud).

properties.name: animationSpriteAssetId
properties.description: Animacion/sprite one-shot que se reproduce al saltar desde una pared. Al terminar, vuelve al sprite base mirando en direccion contraria al muro.

properties.name: slideFallSpeed
properties.description: Velocidad maxima de caida mientras se desliza por la pared. 0 desactiva el slide.

properties.name: lockFrames
properties.description: Frames minimos durante los que se mantiene el impulso horizontal del wall jump. Si la entidad sigue ascendiendo, el impulso se conserva hasta la cima del salto.

properties.name: requirePressAwayFromWall
properties.description: Si es true, exige pulsar la direccion contraria a la pared para saltar.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Activa o desactiva el wall jump para esta entidad.

componentDefinitions.name: Wall Grab
componentDefinitions.description: Permite agarrarse a una pared mientras se mantiene Boton 2/N. Ideal para un control tipo Celeste.

properties.name: grabFallSpeed
properties.description: Velocidad vertical mientras se agarra a la pared. 0 = quedarse quieto, 1+ = deslizarse lentamente.

properties.name: climbSpeed
properties.description: Pixeles por frame al trepar o bajar mientras se mantiene Boton 2/N y se pulsa arriba o abajo.

properties.name: grabDurationFrames
properties.description: Frames maximos de wall grab desde el primer agarre. 240 frames son 4 segundos a 60 FPS.

properties.name: grabSpriteAssetId
properties.description: Sprite que se muestra mientras se esta agarrado a la pared. Si esta vacio, no cambia el sprite.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Activa o desactiva el wall grab para esta entidad.

componentDefinitions.name: Dash
componentDefinitions.description: Define un dash corto y preciso para plataformas tipo Celeste. Es dato de diseño hasta que el runtime/generador lo consuma.

properties.name: dashSpeed
properties.description: Velocidad del dash en pixeles por frame o unidad equivalente del runtime.

properties.name: dashDurationFrames
properties.description: Frames durante los que se mantiene el impulso de dash.

properties.name: dashCooldownFrames
properties.description: Frames antes de permitir otro dash si el runtime lo permite.

properties.name: maxAirDashes
properties.description: Dashes disponibles en el aire antes de tocar suelo o recargar.

properties.name: refillOnGround
properties.description: Recarga el dash al tocar suelo.

properties.name: refillOnWallGrab
properties.description: Recarga el dash al agarrarse a una pared.

properties.name: allowEightDirections
properties.description: Permite dash horizontal, vertical y diagonal.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Activa o desactiva el dash para esta entidad.

componentDefinitions.name: Air Control
componentDefinitions.description: Controla si la entidad puede cambiar su movimiento horizontal mientras esta en el aire.

properties.name: airControlMode
properties.description: Modo de control aereo: full o locked. locked conserva la velocidad horizontal hasta tocar suelo o escalera.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Activa o desactiva esta regla de control aereo.

componentDefinitions.name: Physics

properties.name: velocityX
properties.description: Horizontal speed (fixed-point 8.8 or integer).

properties.name: velocityY
properties.description: Vertical speed (fixed-point 8.8 or integer).

properties.name: friction
properties.description: Damping factor for velocity (0-255, where 255 is no friction).

properties.name: mass
properties.description: Mass of the entity, affecting knockback etc.

componentDefinitions.description: Governs basic physical properties like velocity. Works with Gravity and Jump.

componentDefinitions.name: PlayerInput

properties.name: controllerId
properties.description: Controller ID (0 for player 1, 1 for player 2, etc.).

properties.name: inputEnabled
properties.description: Is input processing active for this entity.

componentDefinitions.description: A marker component indicating the entity responds to player controls.

componentDefinitions.name: AIBehavior

properties.name: aiState
properties.description: Current AI state (e.g., 'idle', 'patrol', 'chase').

properties.name: stateTimer
properties.description: Timer for current AI state duration or cooldown.

properties.name: targetEntityTemplateId
properties.description: ID of the entity template this AI is targeting (e.g., 'tpl_player').

properties.name: patrolRangeX
properties.description: Horizontal patrol range.

properties.name: aggroRadius
properties.description: Radius to detect and target entities.

componentDefinitions.description: Manages autonomous behavior for non-player entities.

componentDefinitions.name: Damage

properties.name: damageAmount
properties.description: Amount of damage dealt.

properties.name: damageType
properties.description: Type of damage (e.g., 'contact', 'bullet', 'explosion').

properties.name: knockbackForce
properties.description: Force applied on hit.

componentDefinitions.description: Defines how much damage an entity inflicts upon collision or attack.

componentDefinitions.name: Deadly Tiles
componentDefinitions.description: Marker component. Enables per-entity detection of deadly behavior-map tiles and updates the runtime flag used by the state machine.

componentDefinitions.name: Collectible

properties.name: itemType
properties.description: Type of collectible (e.g., 'coin', 'key', 'powerup_health').

properties.name: itemValue
properties.description: Value associated with the item (e.g., score, health restored).

properties.name: autoCollectRadius
properties.description: Radius within which the item is automatically collected.

properties.name: collectionSoundRef
properties.description: Sound to play on collection.

componentDefinitions.description: Marks an entity as an item that can be picked up.

componentDefinitions.name: Patrol
componentDefinitions.description: Defines a patrol route for an entity. Works with a Behavior script to update entity velocity.

properties.name: patrolType
properties.description: Type of patrol: Horizontal, Vertical, Box, BackAndForth.

properties.name: waypoint1_x
properties.description: Start X coordinate or min corner of box.

properties.name: waypoint1_y
properties.description: Start Y coordinate or min corner of box.

properties.name: waypoint2_x
properties.description: End X coordinate or max corner of box.

properties.name: waypoint2_y
properties.description: End Y coordinate or max corner of box.

properties.name: patrolSpeed
properties.description: Movement speed during patrol.

properties.name: waypointPause
properties.description: Pause duration in ticks at each waypoint.

properties.name: multiScreen
properties.description: Enable multi-screen patrol (entity moves across multiple screens).

properties.name: originScreenId
properties.description: Screen ID where the entity was created (auto-assigned, used for global coordinates).

componentDefinitions.name: Aiming
componentDefinitions.description: Allows an entity to aim at a target. Used by turrets or enemies that shoot.

properties.name: targetEntityTemplateId
properties.description: The type of entity to aim at.

properties.name: aimingRange
properties.description: Maximum distance to acquire a target.

properties.name: rotationSpeed
properties.description: How fast the entity rotates to face the target (0 for instant).

properties.name: fieldOfView
properties.description: The vision cone angle (0-255, mapping to 0-360 degrees).

properties.name: predictsTargetMovement
properties.description: Whether to aim ahead of a moving target.

properties.name: predictionFactor
properties.description: Multiplier for leading the target.

componentDefinitions.name: Shoot
componentDefinitions.description: Configures a basic projectile shot for an entity (e.g., player/boss/enemy).

properties.name: hasAmmo
properties.description: If false, shooting is disabled (HasAmmo). Manageable from State Machine.

properties.name: spriteAssetId
properties.description: Projectile sprite asset to render (Render).

properties.name: render2
properties.description: Explosion sprite asset to render on impact (Render2). Non-looping animation recommended.

properties.name: offsetX
properties.description: Horizontal offset from shooter center (Offset X).

properties.name: offsetY
properties.description: Vertical offset from shooter center (Offset Y).

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Projectile speed magnitude in px/frame. Used for 4-dir aiming or when velocityX is positive.

properties.name: aimMode
properties.description: Aiming mode: 'facing' (left/right based on mirror) or '4dir' (aim with Arrow keys).

properties.name: allowDiagonals
properties.description: If true and two direction keys are held, shoot diagonally.

properties.name: velocityX
properties.description: Projectile speed on X (px/frame).

properties.name: velocityY
properties.description: Projectile speed on Y (px/frame).

properties.name: range
properties.description: Max travel distance in pixels (distancia de alcance).

properties.name: damage
properties.description: Damage applied on hit (daño).

properties.name: cooldownMs
properties.description: Time between shots in ms (fire rate).

properties.name: fireKey
properties.description: Keyboard code to fire (e.code), defaults to KeyX.

properties.name: expireOnHit
properties.description: If true, projectile despawns on first hit.

properties.name: anchor
properties.description: Spawn anchor relative to shooter (Parent/anchor). Currently informational.

componentDefinitions.name: StateMachine
componentDefinitions.description: Connects an entity to a state machine for behavior control.

properties.name: stateMachineAssetId
properties.description: ID of the state machine asset to use.

properties.name: currentStateId
properties.description: ID of the current active state. Auto-selected from available states.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Whether the state machine is currently active.

componentDefinitions.name: Cursors
componentDefinitions.description: Marks an entity as player-controllable with cursor/arrow keys with configurable allowed directions.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Whether cursor control is active.

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Movement speed in pixels per frame.

properties.name: allowUp
properties.description: Allow movement in UP direction.

properties.name: allowDown
properties.description: Allow movement in DOWN direction.

properties.name: allowLeft
properties.description: Allow movement in LEFT direction.

properties.name: allowRight
properties.description: Allow movement in RIGHT direction.

componentDefinitions.name: Spawner
componentDefinitions.description: Spawns entities at random positions within a defined zone at regular intervals.

properties.name: spawnRate
properties.description: Milliseconds between spawns.

properties.name: maxEntities
properties.description: Maximum entities to spawn simultaneously.

properties.name: spawnZoneX
properties.description: Spawn zone X coordinate in pixels (0 = random across screen).

properties.name: spawnZoneY
properties.description: Spawn zone Y coordinate in pixels (0 = random across screen).

properties.name: spawnZoneWidth
properties.description: Spawn zone width in pixels (0 = full screen width).

properties.name: spawnZoneHeight
properties.description: Spawn zone height in pixels (0 = full screen height).

properties.name: entityTemplateId
properties.description: Template ID of entity to spawn.

properties.name: isActive
properties.description: Whether spawning is currently active.

properties.name: spawnOnStart
properties.description: Spawn an entity immediately when the game starts.

componentDefinitions.name: Tile Collector
componentDefinitions.description: Allows an entity to collect items by walking over specific tiles (Pac-Man style).

properties.name: collectionRadius
properties.description: Pixel radius for tile collection detection.

properties.name: collectibleTileIds
properties.description: Comma-separated list of tile IDs that can be collected.

properties.name: replacementTileId
properties.description: Tile ID to replace collected tiles with (usually empty/floor).

properties.name: collectionSoundId
properties.description: Sound to play when collecting items.

properties.name: targetVariable
properties.description: Optional global variable name to increment when an item is collected (e.g. Score).

properties.name: incrementAmount
properties.description: How much to add to targetVariable on collection. 0 = disabled.

properties.name: flagVariable
properties.description: Optional second global variable to set when an item is collected (e.g. GemsModified).

properties.name: flagValue
properties.description: Value assigned to flagVariable on collection. Use 1 for a pickup flag and clear it later from StateMachine.

properties.name: bonusTileId
properties.description: Optional special tile with its own pickup behavior (kept separate from normal collectibles).

properties.name: bonusReplacementTileId
properties.description: Tile to place after picking up the bonus tile during the current visit. Leave empty to remove it.

properties.name: bonusSoundId
properties.description: Optional sound for the bonus tile pickup.

properties.name: bonusIsPersistent
properties.description: If false, the bonus tile reappears when the screen is reloaded.

properties.name: bonusEntityEffect
properties.description: Optional entity effect for the bonus tile (for now: none or grant_extra_jump).

properties.name: bonusEffectAmount
properties.description: Amount used by bonusEntityEffect (for example, extra jumps granted).

properties.name: bonusSlashStrength
properties.description: Horizontal strength of the bonus slash impulse (used by grant_extra_jump slash behavior).

properties.name: bonusRespawnSeconds
properties.description: 0 = disabled. 1-255 = seconds until the bonus tile respawns after collection.

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Whether tile collection is active.

componentDefinitions.name: Inventory
componentDefinitions.description: Stores collected items and manages inventory state.

properties.name: maxItems
properties.description: Maximum number of items that can be stored.

properties.name: currentItemCount
properties.description: Current number of items in inventory.

properties.name: showCountOnScreen
properties.description: Display item count on screen.

properties.name: countDisplayX
properties.description: Screen X position for count display (in character columns).

properties.name: countDisplayY
properties.description: Screen Y position for count display (in character rows).

properties.name: scorePerItem
properties.description: Score points awarded per collected item.

properties.name: totalScore
properties.description: Total accumulated score.

componentDefinitions.name: Rotate
componentDefinitions.description: Allows an entity sprite to be rotated based on facing direction.

properties.name: rotation
properties.description: Current rotation angle in degrees (0=right, 90=up, 180=left, 270=down).

properties.name: facingDirection
properties.description: Current facing direction (0=right, 1=up, 2=left, 3=down).

componentDefinitions.name: Pac-Man Movement
componentDefinitions.description: Implements advanced Pac-Man style movement with direction intention, tile-based collision checks every 8 pixels, and pixel-perfect movement at 60fps.

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Movement speed in pixels per frame (at 60fps).

properties.name: currentDirection
properties.description: Current movement direction (NONE, LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN).

properties.name: desiredDirection
properties.description: Desired movement direction for next valid turn.

properties.name: pixelCounter
properties.description: Counter for position relative to 8x8 character grid (0-7).

properties.name: velocityX
properties.description: Current horizontal velocity (-speed to +speed).

properties.name: velocityY
properties.description: Current vertical velocity (-speed to +speed).

properties.name: canTurnOnPixel
properties.description: Whether direction changes are allowed on current pixel.

properties.name: stopOnWall
properties.description: Stop movement when hitting wall if no input.

properties.name: allowReverse
properties.description: Allow immediate reverse direction without collision check.

properties.name: tileSize
properties.description: Size of tiles for collision checking (8x8 for MSX).

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Whether Pac-Man movement is active.

componentDefinitions.name: PacmanMovementV2
componentDefinitions.description: Advanced Pac-Man movement system with pixel-perfect collision detection every 8 pixels, direction intention system, and 60fps smooth movement for MSX games.

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Movement speed in pixels per frame at 60fps

properties.name: currentDirection
properties.description: Current movement direction: NONE, LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN

properties.name: desiredDirection
properties.description: Player's desired direction for next turn opportunity

properties.name: pixelCounter
properties.description: Position counter relative to 8x8 character grid (0-7)

properties.name: velocityX
properties.description: Current horizontal velocity (-speed to +speed)

properties.name: velocityY
properties.description: Current vertical velocity (-speed to +speed)

properties.name: canTurnOnPixel
properties.description: Whether direction changes are allowed on current pixel

properties.name: stopOnWall
properties.description: Stop movement when hitting wall if no input pressed

properties.name: allowReverse
properties.description: Allow immediate reverse direction without collision check

properties.name: tileSize
properties.description: Size of tiles for collision checking (8x8 for MSX)

properties.name: isEnabled
properties.description: Whether Pac-Man movement system is active

componentDefinitions.name: PacmanRotationV2
componentDefinitions.description: Automatic sprite rotation based on Pac-Man movement direction with MSX-compatible angles.

properties.name: rotation
properties.description: Current rotation angle: 0=right, 90=up, 180=left, 270=down

properties.name: facingDirection
properties.description: Current facing direction: 0=right, 1=up, 2=left, 3=down

properties.name: autoRotate
properties.description: Automatically rotate sprite based on movement direction

entityTemplates.name: Player Default
entityTemplates.description: Minimal default player with position, render, health and cursor movement.

entityTemplates.name: FakePlayer
entityTemplates.description: Script-driven player lookalike for tutorial/dialog/cutscene screens. It intentionally has no PlayerInput component.

entityTemplates.name: Basic Enemy
entityTemplates.description: A simple enemy that patrols and deals contact damage.

entityTemplates.name: Key Item
entityTemplates.description: A key item to be collected.

entityTemplates.name: Enemy Spawner
entityTemplates.description: Spawns enemies randomly across the screen.

entityTemplates.name: Player Ship
entityTemplates.description: A fast-moving player spaceship with shooting capabilities. Create your own ship sprite and assign it to this entity.

entityTemplates.name: Player Bullet
entityTemplates.description: A fast-moving laser projectile fired by the player ship. Create your own bullet sprite and assign it to this entity.

entityTemplates.name: MSX Platform Player
entityTemplates.description: Minimal MSX Screen 2 platformer player for Mario, Celeste and Metroid-style tests. Uses core movement, tile collision, health and animation components.

entityTemplates.name: MSX Top-Down Player
entityTemplates.description: Minimal top-down Screen 2 player for Pac-Man, maze and adventure tests. Avoids legacy Pac-Man movement duplicates and uses Cursors plus WallCollision.

entityTemplates.name: MSX Shooter Player
entityTemplates.description: Minimal Galaga-style player with cursor movement and the ROM-facing Shoot component.

entityTemplates.name: MSX Projectile
entityTemplates.description: Reusable projectile template for shooter and Metroid-style tests. Includes Damage, Collision and Lifetime for ROM validation.

entityTemplates.name: MSX Basic Patrol Enemy
entityTemplates.description: Minimal enemy for platformer, Metroid and shooter collision tests. Uses Patrol, Damage, Health and WallCollision.

entityTemplates.name: Collector Player
entityTemplates.description: A Pac-Man style player that collects items by walking over tiles. Perfect for maze-based collection games.

entityTemplates.name: Pac-Man Player
entityTemplates.description: Advanced Pac-Man player with pixel-perfect movement, 8-pixel collision checks, direction intention system, and 60fps smooth movement. Sprite size should be 16x16 pixels.

entityTemplates.name: PacmanPlayerV2
entityTemplates.description: Advanced Pac-Man player with pixel-perfect movement, 8-pixel collision checks, direction intention system, and 60fps smooth movement. Optimized for MSX Screen 2 mode with 16x16 sprites.

entityTemplates.name: Box
entityTemplates.description: A movable box that acts as a solid platform. Can be picked up and carried with action key (Z).
